title: Measuring neutrino mass and asymmetry through galaxy pairwise peculiar velocity
summary: Cosmic neutrinos are among the most abundant fermions in the Universe, yet the values of their masses and chemical potentials remain uncertain. In this Letter, we present the first constraints on the total neutrino mass $M_ν$ and the neutrino asymmetry parameter $η^2$ derived from the mean galaxy pairwise peculiar velocity in the quasi-linear and nonlinear regimes. We develop a simulation-based analysis pipeline that connects neutrino properties to predictions of galaxy pairwise velocity, and apply it to galaxy data from the Cosmicflows-4 grouped catalog. Our analysis is performed within two independent cosmological frameworks, based on cosmological parameters derived from Cosmic microwave background (CMB) and local distance ladder measurements, respectively. By performing fits to the galaxy pairwise velocity, we obtain consistent constraints from both frameworks. Quoting posterior means with 68% CL, we find $M_ν= 0.24^{+0.34}_{-0.18}\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $η^2 = 2.14^{+0.30}_{-0.32}$ in the CMB framework, and $M_ν= 0.37^{+0.34}_{-0.26}\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $η^2 = 2.4^{+2.1}_{-1.6}$ in the local framework. In particular, we find a 7$σ$ measurement of a non-zero neutrino asymmetry in the CMB framework. These neutrino parameters are consistent with those, in our previous work, obtained from the Planck CMB temperature power spectrum. These results demonstrate that galaxy pairwise velocities provide an independent and sensitive probe of neutrino properties, opening a new avenue for testing neutrino physics with large-scale structure observations.

AI.tldr: First constraints on total neutrino mass and neutrino asymmetry using galaxy pairwise peculiar velocities, showing consistent results with Planck CMB data and revealing significant neutrino asymmetry.
AI.motivation: Cosmic neutrinos are abundant but their masses and chemical potentials remain uncertain; need independent probes beyond CMB measurements to constrain neutrino properties.
AI.method: Developed simulation-based analysis pipeline connecting neutrino properties to galaxy pairwise velocity predictions, applied to Cosmicflows-4 grouped catalog data within two cosmological frameworks (CMB-based and local distance ladder).
AI.result: Found M_ν = 0.24^{+0.34}_{-0.18} eV and η² = 2.14^{+0.30}_{-0.32} (CMB framework); M_ν = 0.37^{+0.34}_{-0.26} eV and η² = 2.4^{+2.1}_{-1.6} (local framework). 7σ measurement of non-zero neutrino asymmetry in CMB framework.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy pairwise velocities provide independent, sensitive probe of neutrino properties, opening new avenue for testing neutrino physics with large-scale structure observations.

title: Purely Quadratic Non-Gaussianity from Tachyonic Instability: Primordial Black Holes and Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves
summary: We investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation in a cosmological scenario where curvature perturbations follow purely quadratic non-Gaussianity, $ζ= A(φ^2-\langleφ^2\rangle)$, arising from tachyonic instability in multi-component inflationary models. Within an extended Press-Schechter framework based on the compaction function, we derive the probability distribution of the linear compaction function and its asymptotic exponential tail, demonstrating that PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive not only to the amplitude of perturbations but also to the correlation coefficient $ρ$ between the smoothed field and its radial gradient. We further find that, for $A<0$, the spectral width of the curvature power spectrum plays a decisive role in avoiding PBH overproduction: broad spectra yield mildly negative $ρ$ and fail to suppress PBH formation, while sufficiently narrow spectra drive $ρ\to -1$, resulting in an exponential suppression while maintaining a sizable gravitational-wave signal. Thermal inflation provides a useful benchmark scenario with asteroid-mass PBH dark matter and high-frequency scalar-induced gravitational waves potentially detectable by future space-based interferometers, but its typically broad spectra make it challenging to reconcile PTA observations with PBH constraints.

AI.tldr: PBH formation in quadratic non-Gaussian curvature perturbations from tachyonic instability; abundance exponentially sensitive to perturbation amplitude and correlation coefficient ρ; spectral width crucial for avoiding overproduction, with narrow spectra suppressing PBHs while maintaining detectable GW signals.
AI.motivation: Investigate primordial black hole formation in cosmological scenarios with purely quadratic non-Gaussian curvature perturbations arising from tachyonic instability in multi-component inflationary models, particularly examining how PBH abundance depends on perturbation statistics and spectral properties.
AI.method: Extended Press-Schechter framework based on compaction function; derivation of probability distribution of linear compaction function and its asymptotic exponential tail; analysis of correlation coefficient ρ between smoothed field and its radial gradient; examination of spectral width effects on PBH formation.
AI.result: PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to both perturbation amplitude and correlation coefficient ρ; for A<0, spectral width is decisive: broad spectra yield mildly negative ρ and fail to suppress PBH formation, while sufficiently narrow spectra drive ρ→-1, resulting in exponential suppression while maintaining sizable gravitational-wave signals; thermal inflation scenarios face challenges reconciling PTA observations with PBH constraints due to typically broad spectra.
AI.conclusion: Spectral width plays crucial role in PBH formation with quadratic non-Gaussianity; narrow spectra can suppress PBH overproduction while preserving detectable gravitational-wave signals, offering potential resolution for PBH dark matter scenarios; thermal inflation's broad spectra present challenges for reconciling observational constraints.

title: Forecasts of CMB $E$-mode anomalies for AliCPT-1
summary: The standard $Λ$CDM model has been highly successful in describing cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations. Nevertheless, a set of large-scale statistical anomalies persists in temperature anisotropies across WMAP and Planck. CMB $E$-mode polarization offers an independent probe of these anomalies, circumventing the look-elsewhere effect inherent in temperature-only analyses. In this paper, we forecast the capability of the Ali CMB Polarization Telescope (AliCPT), a ground-based CMB experiment in the Northern Hemisphere, to detect such anomalies in large-scale $E$-mode polarization. Using 1000 unconstrained simulations processed with the NILC component separation method, we evaluate four anomaly estimators: dipole modulation, lack of large-angle correlations, quadrupole-octopole alignment, and point-parity asymmetry. Our analysis considers two noise levels for AliCPT, as well as a joint configuration with Simons Observatory (SO) Large Aperture Telescope (LAT). For dipole modulation, we validate the local variance estimator on modulated simulations with an input amplitude $A_d = 0.07$, and find that the combined AliCPT+SO dataset is likely to detect the injected $E$-mode modulation at a 99% confidence level. Tests of the full suite of anomaly statistics on unconstrained isotropic simulations indicate that AliCPT alone, owing to its limited sky coverage, might introduce systematic biases or enlarged uncertainties, especially for quadrupole-octopole alignment and point-parity asymmetry. The combination with SO largely restores the statistical distributions to those expected in an ideal full-sky scenario, thereby establishing a near-cosmic-variance benchmark for upcoming anomaly investigations.

AI.tldr: AliCPT CMB polarization telescope forecasts detection of large-scale anomalies in E-mode polarization, showing combined AliCPT+SO dataset can detect dipole modulation at 99% confidence level.
AI.motivation: The ΛCDM model successfully describes CMB observations, but persistent large-scale statistical anomalies in temperature anisotropies across WMAP and Planck need independent verification using E-mode polarization to avoid look-elsewhere effects in temperature-only analyses.
AI.method: Used 1000 unconstrained simulations processed with NILC component separation method to evaluate four anomaly estimators: dipole modulation, lack of large-angle correlations, quadrupole-octopole alignment, and point-parity asymmetry. Analyzed two noise levels for AliCPT and joint configuration with Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope.
AI.result: For dipole modulation with input amplitude Ad = 0.07, combined AliCPT+SO dataset likely detects E-mode modulation at 99% confidence level. AliCPT alone introduces systematic biases or enlarged uncertainties due to limited sky coverage, especially for quadrupole-octopole alignment and point-parity asymmetry. Combination with SO restores statistical distributions to near-cosmic-variance benchmark.
AI.conclusion: AliCPT's E-mode polarization observations can independently probe large-scale CMB anomalies, with AliCPT+SO combination providing near-cosmic-variance-limited measurements for upcoming anomaly investigations, establishing a robust framework for testing cosmological models.

title: Hamilton's Object Revisited: A challenging source redshift of a strong lensing configuration
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics, comments welcome!
summary: Low-resolution spectrographs used to have difficulties to determine redshifts of galaxies at $z\approx1$ and $z\approx3$. Spectral emission and absorption lines of magnesium and iron redshifted to $z\approx1$ fall close to hydrogen, silicon, and oxygen lines at $z\approx3$. Here, we demonstrate that, even with modern, integrated field unit spectrographs, this task remains challenging. Hamilton's object, a blue star-forming galaxy, gravitationally lensed into three multiple images by the galaxy cluster SDSS J223010.47-081017.8 is such a case. Using the Blue Keck Cosmic Web Imager, its redshift was determined as $z=0.82$, while its MOIRCS spectrum hinted at $z=3.201$. To resolve the ambiguity, we completely re-analyse the Blue KCWI spectra of all three multiple images including the star-forming region in the outskirts. We employ a new data reduction pipeline, PypeIt, signal enhancement, and line fitting by Python-routines. The re-evaluation confirms the previous result based on 6 absorption features, $z=0.820 \pm 0.001$ and 4 emission features, $z=0.821 \pm 0.002$. The alternative $z=3.199\pm 0.003$, based on 6 absorption and 2 emission lines is a worse fit, also compared to other spectra. Moreover, we find the MOIRCS spectrum inconclusive: Observations cover two of three multiple images, with the slit for image C only covering its central bulge; furthermore the pixel-to-wavelength calibration requires a nightsky-emission-line calibration due to a missing calibration arc lamp. New MOIRCS observations are needed to verify that Hamilton's object has the smallest separation in angular diameter distance between lensing cluster and source galaxy among the known cluster-scale strong lenses.

AI.tldr: The paper resolves redshift ambiguity for Hamilton's object, confirming z=0.82 over z=3.20 through reanalysis of KCWI spectra using improved methods, while questioning the MOIRCS spectrum reliability.
AI.motivation: Low-resolution spectrographs historically struggle with redshift determination between z≈1 and z≈3 due to spectral line confusion. Modern IFU spectrographs still face challenges, as demonstrated by conflicting redshift measurements (z=0.82 vs z=3.20) for Hamilton's object, a gravitationally lensed galaxy.
AI.method: Complete re-analysis of Blue KCWI spectra for all three multiple images using new data reduction pipeline (PypeIt), signal enhancement techniques, and Python-based line fitting routines. Includes analysis of star-forming region in outskirts and systematic comparison of absorption/emission line fits.
AI.result: Confirms z=0.820±0.001 from 6 absorption features and z=0.821±0.002 from 4 emission features. Alternative z=3.199±0.003 provides worse fit. MOIRCS spectrum found inconclusive due to partial coverage (only 2 of 3 images), slit placement issues, and calibration problems requiring nightsky-emission-line calibration.
AI.conclusion: Hamilton's object is at z=0.82, not z=3.20. The redshift ambiguity is resolved through improved spectral analysis, though new MOIRCS observations are needed to verify its status as having the smallest angular diameter distance separation among known cluster-scale strong lenses.

title: A population-based approach to understanding radio AGN feedback with LOFAR: The LoTSS Deep Fields
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 14 pages, 6 figures
summary: Feedback from radio AGN jets is regularly implemented into contemporary models of galaxy evolution to offset radiative cooling in the large-scale environments in which they typically reside. While previous studies suggest that the total kinetic power output from radio AGN is sufficient for this purpose, many have relied on jet-power estimation from radio luminosities using generalised scaling relations that neglect additional information such as source size and environment. We here infer the cosmic evolution of radio AGN kinetic jet powers using a physically motivated semi-analytic model for the first time. Initial analysis on a sample of 619 radio AGN at $z < 2.5$ from LoTSS Deep Field and International LOFAR Telescope images of the Lockman Hole implies a population dominated by short-lived sources typically of lower jet power. After incorporating weighting towards shorter lifetimes in the inference models, we utilise ELAIS-N1 and Boötes LoTSS Deep Field data to expand our analysis to a much larger sample of 5,187 objects, deriving jet kinetic luminosity functions and integrated kinetic luminosity densities for the radio AGN population out to $z = 2.5$. In broad agreement with previous results in the literature, we find the total power output per comoving volume to be $\sim$10$^{32}-$10$^{33}$ W Mpc$^{-3}$ across the full redshift range, with some suggestions of moderate positive evolution from $z$ = 0$-$1 and little evolution from $z$ = 1$-$2. These values are compatible with expectations from some cosmological models, providing strong evidence for the viability of feedback from radio AGN jets across cosmic time.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the cosmic evolution of radio AGN jet powers using a physically motivated semi-analytic model on large LOFAR survey data, finding that the total kinetic power output is sufficient for feedback across cosmic time.
AI.motivation: Previous studies of AGN feedback rely on generalized scaling relations from radio luminosities that neglect source size and environmental information. There's a need for physically motivated models to better understand the cosmic evolution of radio AGN kinetic jet powers and their role in galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Developed a physically motivated semi-analytic model for radio AGN jet power estimation, applied to large samples from LoTSS Deep Fields (LoTSS Deep Field, Lockman Hole, ELAIS-N1, Boötes) totaling 5,187 radio AGN at z < 2.5. Incorporated weighting towards shorter lifetimes in inference models.
AI.result: The radio AGN population is dominated by short-lived, lower-power sources. Total kinetic power output is ~10^32-10^33 W Mpc^-3 across z = 0-2.5, with moderate positive evolution from z=0-1 and little evolution from z=1-2. These values are compatible with cosmological model expectations.
AI.conclusion: The study provides strong evidence for the viability of radio AGN jet feedback across cosmic time, with total power output sufficient to offset radiative cooling in large-scale environments as required by galaxy evolution models.

title: Unraveling Chemical Enrichment in Extreme Emission-Line Galaxies: A Multi-Element Bayesian View of Bursty Star Formation and Galaxy Evolution in DESI
summary: Extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs) probe chemical enrichment in low-mass, bursty systems where star formation, feedback, and gas accretion are poorly constrained. Using DESI DR1, we select 23 nearby EELGs with detections of 19 ionic species (S/N $\geq$ 4), stellar masses $ M_* \geq 10^7 M_{\odot}$, and extreme H$α$ and [O III] 5007 equivalent widths (EW $\geq$ 500 Angstrom). We infer non-parametric star-formation histories and fit a Bayesian single-zone chemical-evolution model to O, N, Ne, S, and Ar, allowing time-dependent star-formation efficiency, outflow mass loading, and evolving inflow metallicity. We find short depletion timescales and large mass-loading factors, indicating rapid gas cycling in a burst-driven, non-equilibrium regime, with depletion times below Kennicutt-Schmidt expectations. Star-formation efficiency and outflows are well constrained, while inflow metallicity is weaker due to degeneracies with metal production. Abundance ratios isolate physical drivers: star-formation efficiency sets evolutionary tracks, outflows regulate metal retention and X/O normalization, and inflow metallicity sets baseline enrichment. N/O strongly constrains burst timing and gas flows, Ne/O remains nearly invariant, and S/O and Ar/O show intermediate sensitivity. These results demonstrate that multi-element abundances provide a direct probe of baryon-cycle processes in extreme low-mass starbursts.

AI.tldr: DESI DR1 analysis of 23 nearby extreme emission-line galaxies reveals rapid gas cycling in burst-driven, non-equilibrium systems through multi-element chemical evolution modeling.
AI.motivation: To probe chemical enrichment processes in low-mass, bursty star-forming systems where star formation, feedback, and gas accretion mechanisms are poorly understood and constrained.
AI.method: Selected 23 nearby EELGs from DESI DR1 with detections of 19 ionic species, stellar masses ≥10⁷ M⊙, and extreme Hα and [O III] equivalent widths. Applied non-parametric star-formation histories and Bayesian single-zone chemical-evolution modeling of O, N, Ne, S, and Ar with time-dependent star-formation efficiency, outflow mass loading, and evolving inflow metallicity.
AI.result: Found short depletion timescales and large mass-loading factors indicating rapid gas cycling in burst-driven, non-equilibrium regime. Star-formation efficiency and outflows are well constrained, while inflow metallicity is weaker due to degeneracies. Abundance ratios isolate physical drivers: star-formation efficiency sets evolutionary tracks, outflows regulate metal retention, and inflow metallicity sets baseline enrichment. N/O strongly constrains burst timing and gas flows, Ne/O remains nearly invariant, and S/O and Ar/O show intermediate sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Multi-element abundances provide a direct probe of baryon-cycle processes in extreme low-mass starbursts, demonstrating the power of detailed chemical evolution modeling to constrain star formation, feedback, and gas accretion mechanisms in these extreme systems.

title: Cold molecular gas distribution and kinematics in the low-metallicity dusty starburst of Mrk 996 resolved with ALMA
comment: 12+2 pages, 9 figures, and 5 tables. Submitted to A&A
summary: Detecting cold molecular gas in metal-poor starbursts remains a major challenge. Low carbon and oxygen abundances hinder CO formation, while low dust content reduces shielding against UV photodissociation. Consequently, CO, the main tracer of molecular gas, becomes faint or undetectable. We study the spatial distribution and kinematics of cold molecular gas in Mrk 996, a nearby low-mass Wolf-Rayet galaxy hosting a dense, low-metallicity (about 1/5 solar) and nitrogen-enriched nuclear starburst with complex ionized gas kinematics. Using ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1), we map the morphology and kinematics of the molecular gas and compare them with optical and UV data, tracing the ionized gas and young stellar populations. We detect compact CO clouds within 800 pc of the starburst, spatially offset from the nuclear super star cluster (SSC) and the most highly ionized regions. The CO lines are narrow and supersonic, exhibiting velocity gradients with a mild global blueshift, indicating dynamically perturbed gas without evidence for fast outflows, in contrast with the highly ionized phase. The global CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) ratio is low (R21 ~ 0.3), consistent with subthermal excitation. The millimeter continuum peaks at the SSC, while CO emission is displaced toward obscured regions, suggesting it traces dense shielded clumps. ALMA recovers about half of the single-dish flux, indicating the presence of extended, low-surface-brightness molecular gas. Using a metallicity-dependent CO-to-H2 conversion factor, we infer a molecular gas mass of a few 10^7 solar masses. The molecular gas is only weakly coupled to the stellar feedback that dominates the ionized phase. Our results support a multiphase scenario in which dense molecular clumps survive in shielded regions, while CO is photodissociated in their envelopes, leaving a significant CO-dark H2 component (Abridged).

AI.tldr: ALMA observations of low-metallicity starburst galaxy Mrk 996 reveal compact CO clouds offset from star-forming regions, with low excitation and evidence for significant CO-dark molecular gas.
AI.motivation: To understand how cold molecular gas behaves in metal-poor starburst environments where CO formation is hindered and dust shielding is reduced, making traditional molecular gas tracers unreliable.
AI.method: Used ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) lines to map molecular gas morphology and kinematics, compared with optical/UV data tracing ionized gas and young stars in the nearby low-metallicity Wolf-Rayet galaxy Mrk 996.
AI.result: Detected compact CO clouds within 800 pc of starburst, offset from nuclear super star cluster and highly ionized regions; narrow supersonic lines with mild blueshift gradients; low CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) ratio (~0.3) indicating subthermal excitation; ALMA recovers only half of single-dish flux suggesting extended low-surface-brightness gas; molecular gas mass ~10^7 solar masses using metallicity-dependent conversion factor.
AI.conclusion: Supports multiphase scenario where dense molecular clumps survive in shielded regions while CO photodissociates in envelopes, leaving significant CO-dark H2 component; molecular gas weakly coupled to stellar feedback dominating ionized phase.

title: The fragmentation properties of massive star-forming regions in 30Dor-10 at 2000 au resolution
comment: Accepted for publications in Nature Communications
summary: The fragmentation properties of parsec-scales clumps play a fundamental role in shaping the dense gas condensations known as cores, the immediate progenitor of stars. The distribution of core masses, the so-called core mass function, is the precursor of the stellar initial mass function, which governs the distribution of stellar masses and, consequently, the evolution of galaxies. The stellar initial mass function is often described by a typical Salpeter-like slope, although deviations toward more top-heavy distributions have been reported in extreme environments, raising questions about its universality and about the physical connection between the two mass functions. To date, there are no observational constraints on the core mass function and its link to the initial mass function beyond the Milky Way. Here we present a study of the fragmentation properties and the measurement of the core mass function in an external galaxy, focusing on the 30Dor-10 region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, using high resolution observations that probe spatial scales down to 2000 au. Robust statistical analysis demonstrates that the core mass function is consistent with a Salpeter-like slope and suggests that variations in the stellar mass distribution arise from evolutionary processes rather than from initial fragmentation.

AI.tldr: Study measures core mass function in external galaxy (30Dor-10 in LMC) for first time, finding Salpeter-like slope similar to Milky Way, suggesting stellar IMF variations arise from evolutionary processes rather than initial fragmentation differences.
AI.motivation: To understand the connection between core mass function (CMF) and stellar initial mass function (IMF), particularly whether IMF variations in extreme environments result from different initial fragmentation or evolutionary processes. No previous observational constraints exist on CMF beyond Milky Way.
AI.method: High-resolution observations of 30Dor-10 region in Large Magellanic Cloud probing spatial scales down to 2000 au, enabling study of parsec-scale clump fragmentation and measurement of core mass function in external galaxy.
AI.result: Core mass function in 30Dor-10 region shows Salpeter-like slope, consistent with Milky Way measurements. Robust statistical analysis suggests variations in stellar mass distribution arise from evolutionary processes rather than initial fragmentation differences.
AI.conclusion: First measurement of core mass function beyond Milky Way reveals universal Salpeter-like slope, indicating that observed variations in stellar IMF in extreme environments result from post-fragmentation evolutionary processes rather than differences in initial fragmentation.

title: The core of the problem: Physical limits of the core-Sérsic model
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The core-Sérsic model is the standard tool for describing partially depleted stellar cores in massive early-type galaxies, yet its physical admissibility has rarely been examined. Using numerical deprojections, we show that many formally allowed parameter combinations cannot represent realistic stellar systems: sharp transitions between the inner power-law core and the outer Sérsic profile (large $α$) always generate non-monotonic intrinsic density profiles. We identify, for each set of structural parameters $(γ, m, R_{\text{e}}/R_{\text{b}})$, a critical transition parameter, $α_{\text{crit}}$, above which monotonicity is violated. This threshold systematically depends on the core slope and Sérsic index, implying that a fraction of the commonly used parameter space, including the widely adopted sharp-transition limit $α\rightarrow\infty$, is physically ruled out. These constraints have important consequences for measuring core sizes and mass deficits in massive ellipticals, for constructing dynamical models, and for comparing observations with simulations of supermassive black hole binary evolution.

AI.tldr: The core-Sérsic model, used to describe stellar cores in massive elliptical galaxies, has physically inadmissible parameter combinations that produce non-monotonic density profiles, requiring constraints on transition sharpness.
AI.motivation: To examine the physical admissibility of the core-Sérsic model, which is widely used to describe partially depleted stellar cores in massive early-type galaxies but whose physical validity has rarely been tested.
AI.method: Using numerical deprojections to analyze parameter combinations of the core-Sérsic model, identifying critical transition parameter α_crit for each structural parameter set (γ, m, R_e/R_b) above which monotonicity of intrinsic density profiles is violated.
AI.result: Many formally allowed parameter combinations produce non-monotonic intrinsic density profiles, particularly with sharp transitions (large α). A critical threshold α_crit exists that depends systematically on core slope and Sérsic index, ruling out a fraction of commonly used parameter space including the sharp-transition limit α→∞.
AI.conclusion: The core-Sérsic model requires physical constraints on transition sharpness, with important implications for measuring core sizes and mass deficits, constructing dynamical models, and comparing observations with simulations of supermassive black hole binary evolution.

title: HI 21-cm absorption in low- and high-excitation radio-loud AGNs at $z<0.5$ from MALS
summary: We present results from a search of cold neutral gas associated with radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs) at $z < 0.5$ using HI 21-cm absorption measurements from the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). Cross-matching the MALS 1006 MHz and SDSS DR18 catalogs yields 1908 radio sources at $z < 0.5$. Of these, 613 are classified as AGNs using BPT diagnostics and radio luminosity criteria. We further classify 426 AGNs into 327 low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) and 99 high-excitation radio galaxies (HERGs). We observe a significant ($>3σ$) difference in $k$-corrected $g-r$ color, consistent with LERGs residing in older galaxies with quenched star formation. We searched a radio-bright subsample of 79 LERGs and 20 HERGs ($S_{\mathrm{1.4\,GHz}} > 4$ mJy) for associated HI 21-cm absorption. This spans six decades in radio luminosity ($\log L_{\mathrm{1.4\,GHz}}$ (WHz$^{-1}$) $\sim 21.1-27.0$), probing an order of magnitude fainter than previous targeted HI surveys. We report five new detections (4 LERGs, 1 HERG) at $0.29 < z < 0.47$. The overall detection rate of $3^{+3}_{-2}$% (at a $3σ$ threshold of 10.0 kms$^{-1}$) is consistent with sensitivity-matched low-$z$ ($<0.2$) samples, suggesting no significant redshift evolution out to $z \sim 0.5$ or dependence on radio luminosity. Evaluating velocity offset, asymmetry, and width reveals three systems with entirely redshifted absorption and two with predominantly blueshifted absorption. HI profiles in LERGs show diverse asymmetries and velocity offsets exceeding 350 kms$^{-1}$, indicating disturbed cold-gas kinematics likely driven by lobe expansion or jet activity.

AI.tldr: MeerKAT survey of HI 21-cm absorption in radio-loud AGNs at z<0.5 finds 5 new detections (4 LERGs, 1 HERG) with 3% detection rate, showing no redshift evolution or luminosity dependence, and reveals disturbed cold-gas kinematics in LERGs.
AI.motivation: To search for cold neutral gas associated with radio-loud AGNs at z<0.5 using HI 21-cm absorption, probing fainter radio luminosities than previous surveys and investigating redshift evolution and gas kinematics.
AI.method: Cross-matched MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS) 1006 MHz catalog with SDSS DR18 to identify 1908 radio sources at z<0.5, classified 613 as AGNs using BPT diagnostics and radio luminosity. Selected radio-bright subsample (79 LERGs, 20 HERGs with S_1.4GHz > 4 mJy) for HI 21-cm absorption search spanning six decades in radio luminosity.
AI.result: Found 5 new HI 21-cm absorption detections (4 LERGs, 1 HERG) at 0.29<z<0.47 with overall detection rate of 3^{+3}_{-2}%. Detection rate consistent with low-z samples, suggesting no significant redshift evolution to z~0.5 or luminosity dependence. LERGs show diverse asymmetries and velocity offsets >350 km/s indicating disturbed cold-gas kinematics.
AI.conclusion: HI 21-cm absorption detection rates in radio-loud AGNs show no evolution out to z~0.5 and no dependence on radio luminosity. LERGs exhibit disturbed cold-gas kinematics likely driven by lobe expansion or jet activity, consistent with their residence in older galaxies with quenched star formation.

title: The apparent Large Magellanic Cloud star cluster age gap
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: In the Large Magellanic Cloud, very few clusters have been observed with ages between 4 and 11 Gyr. This phenomenon is sometimes referred to as the `LMC age gap'. We construct a model of the cluster age distribution aiming to reproduce this observation. We linked the star formation history to the cluster initial mass function via a power-law relation between maximum initial cluster mass and global star formation rate. Using a constant cluster forming efficiency of 5%, we then obtained the cluster formation history. Applying a model of cluster mass loss calibrated using N-body simulations and an observational completeness limit, we computed the observable fraction of initially formed clusters and model the cluster age distribution. For a maximum initial cluster mass below $10^5$M$_\odot$ at a star formation rate of 1 M$_\odot$pc$^{-2}$Gyr$^{-1}$, our model reproduced the observed lack of clusters with ages between 4 and 11 Gyr. However, our model required a maximum initial mass at 1 M$_\odot$pc$^{-2}$Gyr$^{-1}$ of at least $2\cdot 10^5$M$_\odot$ in order to reproduce the population of ancient globular clusters. A linear change between maximum initial cluster mass relations from 8 to 12 Gyr reproduced the age gap satisfactorily. In our model, the age gap is a consequence of the star forming history and current observational limits. The age gap corresponds to a period of lower star formation rate, where no clusters with initial mass above approximately 2 to 5$\cdot 10^5$M$_\odot$ were formed. In the present day, these clusters have become so faint that only few of them have been detected. The pattern of both young, bright and old, massive clusters being more easily detectable than clusters of intermediate ages may be more general and not specific to the Large Magellanic Cloud.

AI.tldr: The LMC age gap (4-11 Gyr) is reproduced by modeling cluster formation and evolution, showing it results from lower SFR during that period combined with observational limits - only clusters massive enough to survive and remain detectable are observed.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed scarcity of star clusters in the Large Magellanic Cloud with ages between 4 and 11 Gyr (the "LMC age gap") by developing a model that connects star formation history to cluster formation and evolution.
AI.method: Constructed a model linking star formation history to cluster initial mass function via a power-law relation between maximum initial cluster mass and global star formation rate. Used constant cluster formation efficiency (5%), applied cluster mass loss model calibrated with N-body simulations, and incorporated observational completeness limits to compute observable fraction of initially formed clusters.
AI.result: The model successfully reproduces the LMC age gap when maximum initial cluster mass is below 10^5 M⊙ at SFR of 1 M⊙pc^{-2}Gyr^{-1}. However, to reproduce ancient globular clusters, a higher maximum initial mass (≥2×10^5 M⊙) is required. A linear change in maximum initial cluster mass relations from 8 to 12 Gyr satisfactorily reproduces the age gap.
AI.conclusion: The LMC age gap is a consequence of the star formation history combined with current observational limits. During the gap period (lower SFR), no clusters with initial mass above ~2-5×10^5 M⊙ formed, and those that did form have become too faint for detection. This pattern of detectability favoring young/bright and old/massive clusters over intermediate-age clusters may be general, not specific to the LMC.

title: Photometric Identification of Unresolved Binary Stars in Nearby Open Star Clusters
comment: 24 pages, 13 figures, 4 tables, accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
summary:
This paper introduces a new method to search for unresolved binary stars in open star clusters. The work aims at improving the approach introduced previously, which employs the (H-W2)-W1 versus W2-(BP-K) photometric diagram. This diagram, in tandem with the Gaia Color Magnitude Diagram (CMD) and using theoretical isochrones as reference sequences, is used to estimate the binary star fraction and the distribution of the component mass ratio $q$ in eight nearby open star clusters, including Pleiades, Alpha Per, and Praesepe, which we investigated in previous studies. In this study, to alleviate the uncertainties associated with the use of theoretical isochrones, we propose an empirical isochrones approach. We show that this is an effective approach to exploring a wider primary-mass interval, in particular for the region of low-mass sources.
  Box-and-whisker plots are used to present the distribution of the component mass ratio $q$. The mode of distribution turns out to be in the range $0.43-0.83$ and $0.38-0.63$ for Gaia and infrared-visible photometry, respectively. In addition, we update the algorithm to obtain the binary fraction, whose estimate lies in the range $0.16 - 0.36$ and $0.21 - 0.44$, depending on the adopted method, and show that in previous studies the binary fraction was overestimated. We do not find evidence that the variable spatial resolution of the employed catalogs (Gaia, 2MASS, and WISE) affects the precision of the binary fraction estimate.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an improved method for detecting unresolved binary stars in open clusters using empirical isochrones instead of theoretical ones, allowing better exploration of low-mass sources and providing more accurate binary fraction estimates.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to improve upon previous methods for detecting unresolved binary stars in open clusters by addressing uncertainties associated with theoretical isochrones and extending the analysis to wider primary-mass ranges, particularly low-mass sources.
AI.method: The method employs an empirical isochrones approach using the (H-W2)-W1 versus W2-(BP-K) photometric diagram alongside Gaia Color Magnitude Diagrams. This replaces theoretical isochrones to reduce uncertainties. The approach is applied to eight nearby open clusters including Pleiades, Alpha Per, and Praesepe. Box-and-whisker plots are used to analyze mass ratio distributions, and an updated algorithm calculates binary fractions.
AI.result: The empirical isochrones approach effectively explores wider primary-mass intervals, especially for low-mass sources. Mass ratio distribution modes range 0.43-0.83 (Gaia) and 0.38-0.63 (infrared-visible photometry). Binary fraction estimates range 0.16-0.36 and 0.21-0.44 depending on method, showing previous studies overestimated binary fractions. No evidence found that variable spatial resolution of Gaia, 2MASS, and WISE catalogs affects precision.
AI.conclusion: The empirical isochrones approach provides a more reliable method for studying unresolved binaries in open clusters, particularly for low-mass sources, yielding more accurate binary fraction estimates and revealing that previous studies overestimated binary fractions.

title: Self-regulated galaxy evolution within a self-consistently varying galaxy-wide IMF
summary: Semi-analytical evolution models of galaxies are a useful and computationally inexpensive tool for fast assessment of individual properties and their evolution. In this work, specifically the influence of a metallicity and star-formation rate (SFR) dependent galaxy-wide stellar initial mass function (IGIMF) on the self-regulation of star-formation in a galaxy is of interest. All models -- both non-varying gwIMFs and the IGIMF -- reproduce reasonable gas fractions, gas depletion timescales and the main sequence of star-forming galaxies. However, only the IGIMF model accurately predicts the mass-metallicity relation and provides a more comprehensive description of quenched elliptical galaxies. For massive ellipticals all models suggest the need for an additional gas heating source to reach a quenched state. Using a different stellar yield table in the IGIMF model does not significantly affect the results. In all models, the galaxies evolve self-regulated, determined by the accretion rate. The self-regulated constancy of the SFR reflects the constant SFRs of nearby star-forming galaxies. The specific gas-accretion rate of all galaxies appears to be comparable to the Hubble constant. The inclusion of outflows improves the results for the canonical gwIMF model, but not significantly, while for the IGIMF model it has no significant impact.

AI.tldr: Semi-analytical galaxy evolution models show that a metallicity and SFR-dependent galaxy-wide IMF (IGIMF) accurately reproduces the mass-metallicity relation and elliptical galaxy quenching, while all models require additional gas heating for massive ellipticals.
AI.motivation: To investigate how a metallicity and star-formation rate dependent galaxy-wide stellar initial mass function (IGIMF) affects star-formation self-regulation in galaxies, using semi-analytical models as computationally efficient tools for assessing galaxy properties and evolution.
AI.method: Developed semi-analytical evolution models comparing non-varying galaxy-wide IMFs with the IGIMF approach, examining gas fractions, depletion timescales, main sequence, mass-metallicity relation, and elliptical galaxy quenching. Models included analysis of stellar yield tables and outflow effects.
AI.result: All models reproduce reasonable gas fractions, depletion timescales, and main sequence. Only IGIMF accurately predicts mass-metallicity relation and provides better description of quenched ellipticals. All models require additional gas heating for massive ellipticals. Stellar yield changes don't significantly affect results. Self-regulation determined by accretion rates, with specific gas-accretion rates comparable to Hubble constant. Outflows improve canonical gwIMF results slightly but have no significant impact on IGIMF.
AI.conclusion: The IGIMF model provides superior description of galaxy evolution, particularly for mass-metallicity relation and elliptical quenching. All models demonstrate self-regulated evolution driven by accretion rates, with massive ellipticals requiring additional heating mechanisms. The IGIMF approach offers more comprehensive physical description without significant sensitivity to yield tables or outflows.
